verdicts.tldr: In Rich mode, a document-level fence split at a dedent deletes the user's `[label]: url` code line and renders `#` lines as headings. The ADR's fidelity cost says only that such a line shows a backslash.
verdicts.details:
At markdown.go:404-406, closeFencesAtDedent runs before the bracket walker. Its doc comment (1004-1011) says it writes a closer before the first line indented less than the opener, at document level too. The column-0 lines of ` ```sh
# install
[a]: http://x
make
 ``` ` therefore leave the fence. The walker 'deletes LRD spans entirely' (408-410), so `[a]: http://x` disappears, and `# install` becomes an ATX heading. Line 61 tells the reader such a line 'shows a backslash', and the Rich bullet above it mentions only the split. Neither says that a code line can vanish or that code can turn into a heading. Fix: in line 61's Rich case (and in the sanitize.gno row), say that lines a dedent split moves out of the fence render as markdown and that a definition-shaped line among them is deleted.
verdicts.evidence:
Read at head: markdown.go:404 `if !escapeLeader { s = closeFencesAtDedent(s) }` runs before :412 `walked := escapeBracketsOutsideLinks(s)`. The comment at 408-410 reads 'deletes LRD spans entirely'. The finder's golden pins output.md ` ```sh / ```/# install/make/ ```/ ``` ` with no `[a]` line, and output.html `

install

make

` between two empty `
`. Not rerun: this judge writes nothing to the worktree.
verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b3-lines-removed-reach-catalog-dedent-split-deletes-lrd.txtar gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/golden/sanitize/ && go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown -run 'TestSanitizeIntegration/b3-lines-removed-reach-catalog-dedent-split-deletes-lrd' -v: passes with output.md missing the `[a]: http://x` line

verdicts.tldr: With `[home](` followed by `<gno-a b>)` on the next line, the user's `home` links to the realm's own `[home]` URL instead of the user's destination.
verdicts.details: scanLinkURL (1466-1472) skips at most one line ending, then accepts `<gno-a b>` as a pointy destination, so the walker at :412 keeps `[home](\n<gno-a b>)` as a link and leaves its brackets alone. The per-line loop then reaches :476 `line = escapeGnoExtDelimiters(line)`, sees `<gno-` at block start, and writes `\<gno-a b>)`. Goldmark reads `\<gno-a` as a plain destination followed by `b>)`, which is not a title, so the inline link fails and `[home]` binds to the realm's definition as a shortcut reference. The base fails the same way: its walker ran at base:397 and its line-start escape at base:434. The comment at :383-390 shows that this PR moved the `<gno-button` escape before the walker for exactly this shape, but it left the generic `<gno-…>` escape after the walker. The class was swept and this member was missed. Fix: run the block-start `<gno-…>` escape before escapeBracketsOutsideLinks, as escapeGnoButtonTags already is, and add a `[home](\n<gno-a b>)` row next to markdown_test.go:258.
verdicts.evidence: Read at head: :391 `s = escapeGnoButtonTags(s)` comes before :412 `escapeBracketsOutsideLinks(s)`, which comes before :476 `escapeGnoExtDelimiters(line)` inside `for idx, line := range lines`. scanLinkURL :1468 is `skipSpace(s, i, 1, budget)`, then `if s[i] == '<'`. markdown_test.go:258 pins only the one-line `[home](<gno-a b>)`. Base: :397 walker, :434 line-start escape in the loop. The finder's run shows BlockRich `[home](\n<gno-a b>)` bound-to-realm=true own-dest=false. Not rerun here.
verdicts.verify_by: Copy tests/b1-removed-claims-pointy-dest-quote_test.go to gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/zz_pointy_dest_quote_test.go and run go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown -run TestPointyDestOnQuoteContinuation -v at a8bdd53b0 and at d25b308c1; a fix moves escapeGnoExtDelimiters before escapeBracketsOutsideLinks as escapeGnoButtonTags was

verdicts.tldr: Decision 7's calibration shape is written with raw line breaks inside a code span, so readers see `[a]: u (x ` instead of the shape. The unclosed backtick fragments that follow pair up with the wrong backticks.
verdicts.details:
Lines 41-43 read 'calibration shape `[a]: u' / '(x' / '`, both timed …'. A code span turns its line endings into spaces, so it renders `[a]: u (x `. Everywhere else, line 43 and line 63 included, the ADR writes the same shape as `[a]: u
(x
`. On line 43, both 'then `
 to the end' and '+ `
 to the end' open a backtick with no closer of their own, so each one pairs with the next backtick on the line and the prose between them renders as code. Fix: write `[a]: u
(x
` on line 41 and close the two `
` spans on line 43 (`
` + ' to the end').
